intro: Prague rewards slow wanderers with hidden courtyards, grand squares, and river views at every turn. Pick how long you have and what you enjoy most.
tour_note: Check the tour page for which entry tickets are included.

notes: Metro has 3 lines (A, B, C) and runs roughly 05:00–24:00.
Trams cover the centre well; buy tickets at yellow machines or in apps.
A 90-minute ticket costs about 50 CZK; a 24-hour ticket about 150 CZK.
Ride apps Uber and Bolt work in Prague; use them to avoid taxi touts.
Driving in the centre is slow and parking is restricted; use P+R lots.
The centre is walkable; Charles Bridge and Old Town are best on foot.

charles_bridge.name: Charles Bridge
charles_bridge.tip: Come before 08:00 or after 20:00 to see it without the crowds.

prague_castle.name: Prague Castle
prague_castle.price_text: ≈ CZK 250–450 for main circuit; grounds free
prague_castle.hours: Grounds daily 06:00–22:00 · buildings usually 09:00–17:00, check on the day
prague_castle.tip: Walk up through the castle gardens or take tram 22 to save the climb.

old_town_square.name: Old Town Square
old_town_square.tip: The square is best at dusk when the church and clock light up.

st_vitus.name: St. Vitus Cathedral
st_vitus.price_text: Included in Prague Castle circuit ticket (≈ CZK 250–450)
st_vitus.hours: Usually 09:00–17:00, shorter on Sundays; check on the day
st_vitus.tip: Go first thing in the morning; the queue grows fast by mid-morning.

astronomical_clock.name: Prague Astronomical Clock
astronomical_clock.price_text: Free to watch outside; tower climb ticketed
astronomical_clock.tip: Arrive 10 minutes early for a spot; the show lasts under a minute.

petrin_tower.name: Petřín Lookout Tower
petrin_tower.hours: Usually 10:00–18:00, longer in summer; check on the day
petrin_tower.tip: Take the funicular up and walk down through the orchards.

tyn_church.name: Church of Our Lady before Týn
tyn_church.landmark: Church of Our Lady before Týn
tyn_church.hours: Usually Tue–Sun afternoons; closed Mondays, check on the day
tyn_church.tip: The twin spires are best photographed from the Old Town Square side at dusk.

dancing_house.name: Dancing House
dancing_house.price_text: Free to see outside; rooftop bar has a minimum spend
dancing_house.tip: View it from the riverbank across the street for the full shape.

aquapalace.name: Aquapalace Prague
aquapalace.price_text: ≈ CZK 600–900 depending on duration; check online
aquapalace.tip: Book online for a discount and go on a weekday to avoid queues.

clementinum.name: Clementinum National Library
clementinum.hours: Daily roughly 09:00–19:00; check on the day
clementinum.tip: Tours run in groups; the Baroque Library Hall is the highlight.

devils_channel.name: Devil's Channel Cruise
devils_channel.hours: Daytime departures, weather permitting; check on the day
devils_channel.tip: Small boats go into the narrow channel; sit near the front for views.

dinopark.name: Dinopark (Prague)
dinopark.hours: Usually 09:00–18:00 in season; check on the day
dinopark.tip: Good for families with kids; combine with a walk along the river.

estates_theatre.name: Estates Theatre
estates_theatre.hours: Performances usually evenings; box office daytime
estates_theatre.tip: Mozart premiered Don Giovanni here; book ahead for opera nights.

jewish_quarter.name: Jewish Quarter
jewish_quarter.hours: Sites usually 09:00–18:00, closed Saturdays and Jewish holidays
jewish_quarter.tip: Buy the combined ticket; the Old Jewish Cemetery is the most moving stop.

karlstejn.name: Karlštejn Castle
karlstejn.hours: Usually Tue–Sun 09:00–17:00 in season; closed in winter, check on the day
karlstejn.tip: A half-day trip by train from Prague; book the tour slot in advance.

lesser_town.name: Lesser Town
lesser_town.tip: Wander the lanes below the castle; quieter than the Old Town.

national_theatre.name: National Theatre of Czech
national_theatre.hours: Performances usually evenings; box office daytime
national_theatre.tip: The building itself is worth a look; opera and ballet tickets sell out early.

powder_tower.name: Powder Tower
powder_tower.hours: Usually 10:00–18:00 in season; check on the day
powder_tower.tip: It marks the old city gate; climb for a view over the Old Town roofs.

lunapark.name: Prague Lunapark
lunapark.price_text: Free entry; rides paid per ride
lunapark.hours: Seasonal, usually daytime to evening; check on the day
lunapark.tip: A fun stop with kids; check it is open before you go.

prague_zoo.name: Prague Zoo
prague_zoo.hours: Usually 09:00–18:00 in season; check on the day
prague_zoo.tip: Allow half a day; take the bus from the metro to the main gate.

rudolfinum.name: Rudolfinum
rudolfinum.hours: Concerts usually evenings; box office daytime
rudolfinum.tip: Home of the Czech Philharmonic; check the concert calendar early.

strahov_library.name: Strahov Monastery Library
strahov_library.tip: The Philosophical Hall is stunning; you view it from the doorway only.

naplavka_market.name: Náplavka Farmers' Market
naplavka_market.price_text: Free entry; food paid per item
naplavka_market.hours: Usually Saturday mornings; check on the day
naplavka_market.tip: Riverside food stalls on Saturdays; grab a snack and sit by the water.

letna_viewpoint.name: Letná Park viewpoint
letna_viewpoint.tip: Great free view over the bridges; bring a drink at sunset.

beer_tour.name: Czech beer tasting tour
beer_tour.tip: A guided walk with tastings in a few pubs; check what is included.

vinohrady_walk.name: Vinohrady neighbourhood walk
vinohrady_walk.tip: Quiet streets, cafés and parks away from the crowds; good for a slow afternoon.

river_cruise.name: Vltava river sightseeing cruise
river_cruise.hours: Daytime and evening departures; check on the day
river_cruise.tip: An easy way to see the bridges and castle from the water.

stays.why: Steps from Old Town Square and Charles Bridge. Walk to most sights; noisier at night.
Quiet cobbled lanes under the castle. Romantic and close to the bridge; fewer trams.
Leafy, local and full of cafés and restaurants. Good value; 15–20 minutes by tram or metro to the centre.
Central and practical around Wenceslas Square. Main train station and metro nearby; busy streets.

food: Try Czech classics: svíčková (beef in cream sauce), goulash with bread dumplings, and fried cheese.
Prague is famous for beer. A half-litre of local lager is often cheaper than a coffee; prices vary by pub.
Snack on a trdelník (chimney cake) from a street stall, or grab a chlebíček open sandwich from a deli.
Lunch menus (polední menu) at local pubs are the best value: a soup and main for a modest price.
Book popular dinner spots ahead for weekends. Many kitchens close early on Sunday.
more_time: Day trip to Kutná Hora: train from the main station, about an hour each way, to see the bone church and old town.
Swap one museum for a half-day at Vyšehrad: fortress walls, a cemetery of famous Czechs and river views.
Take a tram to Letná or Petřín for a park walk and a beer garden with a city view.
